question: Where should a browser SPA store access tokens, and what attack trade-offs exist between localStorage and httpOnly cookies?
shortAnswer: localStorage is easy for XSS theft; httpOnly secure cookies mitigate XSS token theft but need CSRF defenses. Prefer short-lived access tokens and careful threat modeling.
strongAnswer: XSS can read localStorage/sessionStorage, so long-lived tokens there are risky. httpOnly Secure SameSite cookies are not readable by JS, reducing XSS token exfiltration, but cookie-based auth needs CSRF protections (SameSite, anti-CSRF tokens) and correct domain/path scoping. Many teams use short-lived access tokens in memory plus refresh rotation. Align with OWASP session guidance and your threat model.
advancedAnswer: Cover BFF patterns, token binding, refresh rotation/reuse detection, and mobile secure storage differences.
followUps: How does SameSite=Lax behave on top-level GET?
What changes for native mobile apps?
commonWrongAnswer: JWT in localStorage is always fine if the API uses HTTPS.
productionRelevance: Auth mistakes are high-impact in fintech and SaaS—frequent senior interview territory.
